newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK paper - Japan warns investor pullout possible.
newsitem.headline: HK paper - Japan warns investor pullout possible.

text.p: Japan has warned that Japanese investors might pull out of Hong Kong if the colony's economic autonomy and the rule of law were undermined after its transfer to Chinese sovereignty in mid-1997, the South China Morning Post said on Monday.

The newspaper quoted unidentified sources as saying this message was delivered by Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda last week when he met Acting Governor Anson Chan during his visit to Hong Kong.
Ikeda told Chan that Japanese investments -- now ranked second after China -- would remain in Hong Kong if the systems that made the territory tick were retained, the newspaper said.
The same message was also delivered to China's top policymaker on Hong Kong, Lu Ping, when he visited Japan in June, it said.
Japanese investments in Hong Kong totalled US$14.3 billion as of March 1995, according to Consulate-General of Japan.
Hong Kong's top trade representative in Japan, David Lan, told the Post that there had always been some concern and fears among Japanese businessmen over the fate of the colony.
"It's important that they do speak out frankly about their concerns ... after all the "one country, two systems' policy is a novel idea and untried," Lan said.
After more than 150 years of colonial rule, Hong Kong will revert to China at midnight on June 30 next year as an autonomy region, the Special Administrative Region of China.
